reviewMethod: Independent visual sweep of all 32 paper pages and scheme pages 1–2 and 24–52. Each required task reconciled with its detailed mark allocation, including shared parts, printed answer choices and all diagrams. Final question/solution crops inspected before publication.
sourceNotes: All ten questions retained: 54 tasks, 380 offered marks. Q4(a)(ii) and (iii) share one 5C allocation and remain one card.
Paper 2 has 5B (0,3,5), 5C (0,3,4,5), 10C (0,4,6,10), unlike Paper 1. Q7(b) detailed scheme explicitly uses 15D (0,5,8,12,15), overriding the general table’s 4-mark low-credit band.
Q1(a)(iii) requires every product with exactly one ordered dice outcome: 1,9,16,25,36. The five answers are not a selectable subset.
Q2(b) samples the full birth register. Both probabilities have denominator 55,959; the female subtotal is not the denominator for part (ii).
Q4(b)(ii) requires two points on each circle. These are open mathematical examples, not a fixed finite question pool; all four requested points stay on one 5C card.
Q5(e) is one answer-selection task with six printed alternatives and a reason; all alternatives remain on one card. Q5(c)–(d) retain the original plotted example and its line of best fit.
Q6(b) construction retains the given point, full drawing area, model triangle, compass arcs and ±0.25 cm tolerance. Q6(c) rejects x=4 because a side would be negative.
Q7(b) has nine ordinates including the zero at A: 0,30,35,40,45,30,25,30,40 at 20 m intervals. Their interior sum is 235 and area 5100 m².
Q7(d) rounds upwards to 20 complete laps to reach at least 5 km. Q7(e) uses 2 mm = 0.2 cm for each bead and gives 46⅔% empty space (46.7% in the scheme).

Q8(a)(iii): the source uses x for the remaining distance, then correctly concludes the boat moves 251 m. The paper’s x is the distance moved: x=500−31.7/tan(2A). A clarification distinguishes the variables.

Q9(e) requires both walkers’ positions, (2,3) and (2,5), at the instant Alice and Ciara meet; Brian and Dave have not yet met. Q9(f) is not a square: adjacent slopes are not perpendicular and the diagonals have different lengths.

Q10(a)(i) uses range to mean minimum-to-maximum intervals in its model. Retain petrol 156–213 cents and diesel 145–205 cents. The ordinary statistical ranges 57 and 60 cents are correct differences but receive high partial credit in this scheme.
Q10(a)(ii) uses population standard deviation, 18.9976 cents, rounded to 19; mean 177.9167 rounds to 178. All eight months within one standard deviation remain in part (iii).

Q10(b)(ii) rounds 740/1276×100 early to 57.99, producing printed limits 55.191% and 60.789%. Retaining precision gives 55.194% and 60.793% to 3 decimal places, or proportion limits 0.552 and 0.608. A labelled NextStepUni worked example shows the calculation; official credit notes remain unchanged.
